concept.name: Smoothed moving average
concept.definition: A recursive moving average (also called modified or running moving average) equivalent to an EMA with smoothing constant 1/n, so it smooths far more heavily than a same-length standard EMA.
concept.intuition: The gentlest common average: each new price is absorbed at only 1/n weight, so the line moves slowly and filters a great deal of noise.
concept.mechanics: Seeded with an n-period SMA; thereafter SMMA_t = (SMMA_{t-1}*(n-1) + P_t)/n. This is the smoothing Welles Wilder used for RSI, ATR, and ADX, and the average used in Bill Williams' Alligator lines.
concept.formula: SMMA_t = (SMMA_{t-1} * (n - 1) + P_t) / n; first value = SMA of the first n prices.
concept.failure_modes: Very heavy lag; early values depend strongly on the seed and need long histories to stabilize, so short data sets give unreliable readings.
concept.misconceptions: SMMA(n) is not the same as EMA(n): its alpha is 1/n rather than 2/(n+1), so a 14-period SMMA responds roughly like a 27-period standard EMA.
concept.example: If the prior 14-period SMMA is 50 and the new close is 52, SMMA = (50*13 + 52)/14 = 50.14.
